answers.docs.gaps:
a) Missing, and it is the central gap for this archetype: nothing in docs/
states whether the registry names are visible to MiniJinja's `{% include %}`
as *registry* names. docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md shows only
`{% include "partials/header.jinja" %}` — with an extension, and as a literal.
Meanwhile docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md says a command's template name has
"**no extension appended**" (`pr.checks.list` → `pr/checks/list`), and
docs/crates/render/topics/file-system-resources.md says "A lookup tries the
given name exactly first; if that carries one of the extensions above, it also
tries the name with that extension stripped." Those three passages together
imply the include name goes through the same registry lookup, but no page says
so. Empirically it does: `{% include name %}` resolves `ok` (registry name) and
`ok.jinja` (extension stripped and retried) identically, and a name that is not
registered raises `tried to include non-existing template "okk"`. A sentence in
templating.md's "Including Templates" section stating that includes resolve
through the template registry, extension-optionally, and error when absent,
would have removed the only guess in this build.

b) Wrong-ish / stale: docs/topics/app-configuration.md's "Default Command"
section shows `.command("list", list_handler, "{{ items | length }} items")` —
a three-argument `command` taking a template *string*. The same page's own
"Command Registration" section documents `command_with(path, impl Handler,
|cfg| …)`, and docs/guides/intro-to-standout.md documents the same. I did not
use `.command(...)`, so I did not verify the arity, but the two sections of one
page disagree on the registration API.

c) Missing: docs/topics/standout-help.md documents `-h`/`--help`/`help`, and
says a `help` deeper in the tree is the application's own ("`myapp db help` is
yours"), but never says how to reach a *subcommand's* help through the word.
`validity help nest inner leaf` works and renders the leaf page; that spelling
is only implied by clap's stock about-string ("Print this message or the help
of the given subcommand(s)"), which the same page quotes as a table cell rather
than as documented behavior.

d) Cosmetic, at the level of the rendered page: the root help USAGE block comes
out as two lines with the second indented under the first —

    USAGE
      validity [OPTIONS]
           validity [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

That is clap's multi-line usage string dropped into standout's single-line
`[usage]` slot, so the continuation keeps clap's own "Usage: "-width padding
and does not line up with the template's two-space indent. Nothing in
standout-help.md's `usage` variable description ("Usage line (without "Usage: "
prefix)") anticipates a multi-line value. Also, subcommand help renders its
usage as the bare leaf name (`USAGE  leaf`) rather than the full invocation
path `validity nest inner leaf`, which is what clap itself would print.
answers.friction:
a) The main one: docs/ has no API for choosing a template at run time. SPEC
item 2 requires `show <name>` to treat `<name>` as a registry name, but every
registration path in docs/ fixes the template at build time —
docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md: "`template_name` | `template_name = "…"` |
Names the template registry entry instead of using the convention", and
docs/topics/app-configuration.md: "With no `.template_name(...)` set on the
`CommandConfig`, the template resolves by convention: the command path with
`.` replaced by `/`". Nothing on `CommandConfig`, `CommandContext`, `Output`,
or the hook phases takes a per-invocation template name.

The obvious workarounds are both blocked by the docs themselves: rendering
inside the handler with `Renderer::render` needs the output mode, and
docs/topics/output-modes.md says "Output mode is a rendering concern and is
deliberately absent from `CommandContext`". I landed on a one-line template,
`{% include name %}`, which keeps resolution in the framework's own render
pass — but I got there by inference from the partials example, not from a
documented seam.

b) The not-found diagnostic doubles its prefix:

    $ validity show okk
    template not found: template not found: tried to include non-existing template "okk" (in show:1)

Correct behavior (exit 1, empty stdout, the name is there), but the message
reads as if two layers each prepended "template not found: ".

c) Recursion produces a diagnostic that loses the cause:

    $ validity show show
    could not render include: error in "show" (in show:1)

Exit 1 and no hang, which is what matters, but "error in "show"" does not say
it was recursion.

d) Not standout's fault, but it shaped my probing: the sandbox blocks `/tmp`
and `$HOME/.cargo`, so `2>/tmp/err` fails with "operation not permitted" and
`cargo` had to populate a fresh CARGO_HOME. Every build also emits a spurious
`warning: output of `xcrun` while finding MacOSX.sdk … errno=Operation not
permitted`.

answers.summary:
`validity`, a single-binary standout 9.0.0 app in `app/`. It builds clean
(`cargo build`; the only warning is the sandbox's xcrun cache noise, not code)
and I verified every user-facing line in SPEC.md by running the binary.

Shape:

- `src/main.rs` — clap `Command` built with the builder API (`show <NAME>`,
  `early`, `late`, `nest inner leaf`, with `nest` and `nest inner` marked
  `subcommand_required`), four `#[handler]` adapters, and an `App::builder()`
  chain whose ordering is the construction contract:
  `.command_with("early", …)` is called *before* `.templates(...)`/`.styles(...)`
  and `.command_with("late", …)`, `.command_with("show", …)`,
  `.command_with("nest.inner.leaf", …)` after them. `build()` runs before
  `verify_command` and `run`.
- `src/templates/ok.jinja` — `[ok]ok[/ok]` plus a trailing newline. Registry
  name `ok`. `early`, `late` and `nest inner leaf` render it directly via
  `cfg.template_name("ok")`.
- `src/templates/show.jinja` — `{% include name %}`. This is how `show`
  resolves a registry name: the handler returns only `{ name }` view data and
  the render pass resolves the requested template. There is no `match` on the
  string anywhere in the application.
- `src/styles/app.css` — defines `.ok` and nothing else. No help/topic tags,
  help handling left at its default.

Observed behavior (all checked against the built binary):

- `show ok`, `early`, `late`, `nest inner leaf` under `--output text` and
  piped-auto each write exactly `6f 6b 0a` (`ok\n`) to stdout, exit 0, empty
  stderr. `--output term` gives `\x1b[32m\x1b[1mok\x1b[0m\n` — visible text
  still `ok`, no `[ok?]`.
- `show okk` and `show nosuch`: empty stdout, exit 1, immediate, stderr names
  the requested template (`tried to include non-existing template "okk"`). No
  `{{`, no `{%`, no name-as-body.
- Help at the root and at `nest inner leaf` via `help`, `--help`, `-h` (and
  `help nest inner leaf`): exit 0, stdout, empty stderr, no `[about?]`
  `[header?]` `[usage?]` `[item?]` `[metavar?]` `[desc?]` `[default?]`
  `[values?]` `[example?]` markers in any mode. Root help carries a USAGE line
  and names `show`, `early`, `late`, `nest`; leaf help names `leaf`.

answers.workarounds:
a) `src/templates/show.jinja` is a second registered template, `{% include name %}`.
SPEC item 1 is headed "One registered application template", and strictly there
are two registry entries: `ok` (the application's content template, the only one
that renders text) and `show` (one line of dispatch plumbing that exists only
because the framework fixes template names at build time — see friction (a)).
The spec's explicit prohibition is only on registering `okk` or `nosuch`, and
neither exists. I could not find a way to satisfy item 2 with a single entry:
`show` must render *something*, and that something cannot be `ok` without making
`show nosuch` succeed.

b) `show`'s failure diagnostic is the framework's, not the application's. I
deliberately did not add an application-side existence check that would produce
a nicer message, because any such check would need its own list of valid names
and would be exactly the "match on the string in application code" the spec
forbids. The cost is that the wording of the exit-1 stderr line is standout's to
change — it names the template today (verified), but the application does not
guarantee it.

c) `app.verify_command(&command)` runs on every invocation rather than in a
test. docs/topics/standout-help.md and docs/topics/dispatch-attributes.md both
frame it as a setup/test-time check, but this app ships no test suite, so
running it in `main` is what keeps a handler/argument drift loud instead of a
runtime `get_flag` panic. It passes on every path I exercised, including all
help forms.

d) `OkView` is an empty `#[derive(Serialize)]` struct for the three commands
that render `ok` and read no data, so `--output json` on `early`/`late`/`leaf`
returns `{}`. The spec does not pin structured output for those commands.
